summary: A coarse optical-flow ridge model ran end to end but was rejected: it improved normalized delta RMSE while regressing every physical translation, rotation, gripper, and integrated-trajectory metric against zero-delta and train-mean controls.
evidence: The frozen split used clean_table/fold_shirt/pour_water for training, pour_over_coffee for validation, and wipe_table for test.
Video ridge translation-delta RMSE was 0.5101 cm versus 0.3977 cm for zero delta; rotation-delta geodesic error was 12.9393 degrees versus 4.4345 degrees.
Only two physical test episodes were present after grouping four clips by source lineage; promotion_eligible was false.
lessons: A global flow summary can reduce a scale-normalized proxy while worsening metric robot-base motion; physical metrics must remain primary.
Compiled clips cannot be counted as independent episodes when two clips share one physical source episode.
limitations: The pilot has one camera rig, one embodiment, one test task, and two independent test episodes.
It predicts realized EEF state changes, not low-level commands, contact, or phase.
next_actions: Try a spatially resolved representation once; stop ridge tuning if physical metrics still regress and pivot to calibrated geometry/semantic tracking.
